newsitem.title: USA: Atlas buys 10 Boeing freighter jets.
newsitem.headline: Atlas buys 10 Boeing freighter jets.

text.p: Atlas Air Inc said on Monday it had a definitive agreement to purchase 10 freighter jets from Boeing Co.
Under the terms of the agreement, Atlas will purchase 10 new Boeing 747-400 freighter aircraft, with the option to purchase an additional 10, the company said.

Delivery of the first 10 aircraft will take place during a four-year period beginning in 1998, it said. The delivery schedule has been established for four aircraft in 1998, two aircraft in 1999, three aircraft in 2000 and the tenth aircraft in 2001.
The company said it expected to place the aircraft with its existing and prospective customers.

"The aircraft will expand our ability to service our customers in global markets creating a competitive advantage for Atlas which we believe will significantly enhance our shareholder value," Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Chowdry said in a statement.

Atlas said the 747-200 aircraft will continue to be a mainstay. However, it said it has come to believe that adding the 747-400 to its fleet will better service many of its existing and potential customers. The 747-400 burns less fuel, has longer range and greater payload capability than the 747-200.

"These aircraft will serve as replacements for the five FedEx aircraft currently on lease through the end of this year thereby eliminating inefficient aircraft with limited customer application from our fleet," President and Chief Operating Officer Mickey Foret said in a statement.

Foret added, "We believe that this acquisition will not only reduce Atlas' operating costs for the next decade, but it will also provide new aircraft for those markets where new aircraft are preferred."
